context.why:
This package is a user-interface layer over payment backends. Its drf-stripe namespace already contributes three pages to django-mvp's Account Center; the subscription page was filled in by the previous feature and the Plans page is still an empty heading. This story fills it, and it fills it with the payment provider's own embeddable pricing table rather than markup of ours.

That choice was made at the specification gate and is not yours to revisit. What it means concretely: you build one Cotton component that emits the provider's `<stripe-pricing-table>` custom element and its attributes, and a view that hands that component two values read from the project's settings. You build nothing that knows what a plan costs. No amount, no currency, no billing frequency, no plan name is produced anywhere by this package — every price a reader sees is rendered by the provider inside its own frame.

The component takes its values as attributes and reads no settings, because a project must be able to place it on any page of its own. The shipped Plans page is the one that reads settings, because nobody is passing it attributes — a project writes no template for that page, which is the whole point of it.

This story stops short of four things that belong to later stories, and you must not build them: the signed-in person's email address (US-2), the placement on the demonstration project's landing page (US-3), the state where nothing is configured yet (US-4), and the override documentation and constitution amendment (US-5).

prior_decisions: The provider's embed is the default and no plan selection is built from the backend's records. The maintainer ruled on this at the specification gate. Do not build a plan grid, do not read Price or Product, do not touch the backend's models at all — this story reads two settings and nothing else.

The script element is never emitted. Article XIII of CONSTITUTION.md: a package that injected a script tag would add a third-party origin to every project that installed it. The component emits the mount point; the host project loads the library however it already manages its frontend. T004 makes this a repository-wide test so it stays true for every template added after yours.

The page may read a publishable key from settings and the component may not. The split preserves the property those rules exist for: the component stays free of hidden configuration so it renders anywhere a template author places it. CONSTITUTION.md still carries the older, stricter wording — narrowing it is T032 in US-5, NOT your task. Do not edit CONSTITUTION.md in this story.

A publishable key is not a secret. It identifies an account, the provider prints it in its own copy-paste examples, and it is designed to sit in markup a browser downloads. Treat it as configuration, and never confuse it with an API key or a webhook signing secret, which remain forbidden everywhere in this package.
WATCH — The design review returned approve with zero findings, so you carry no watch items from it.

WATCH — The word 'Plans' appears in the Account Center's navigation as well as on the page itself, and django-mvp draws that navigation twice. tests/markup.py exists to narrow an assertion to one region — use it rather than counting a string across the whole page.

WATCH — Settings are read at render time, never at import. tests/settings_without_backend.py and the existing SubscriptionPageView show the shape: getattr(settings, 'MVP_PAYMENTS', {}).get(...). T003 is the test that holds this.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the component rendered in a bare template with table_id and publishable_key, when the output is read, then it contains a stripe-pricing-table element carrying pricing-table-id and publishable-key with those values, contains no '<script' anywhere, and contains no figure that could read as an amount.

Given a project with both settings supplied, when a signed-in person opens the Plans page, then the page's context carries pricing_table_id and publishable_key and its content region renders the provider's element with both; and the rendered page contains no script element referencing the provider; and a visitor who is not signed in is redirected to the sign-in page.
Given MVP_PAYMENTS absent from settings entirely, when the Plans page renders, then nothing raises; and importing mvp_payments.views with settings unconfigured raises nothing.
Given every template shipped under mvp_payments/templates/, when each is read, then none contains a script element with a src attribute pointing at any host.
Given the component file exists, when it is rendered, then it emits only the provider's element and its two attributes — no script, no style, no wrapper this story does not need.

Given PlansPageView, when it builds its context, then pricing_table_id and publishable_key are read from settings.MVP_PAYMENTS at render time, each defaulting to None, and its docstring names both as the surface a project overriding the page relies on.
Given the drf-stripe contribution, when its Plans page is routed, then it uses PlansPageView; and the subscription and billing pages keep routing exactly as they do now.
Given the Plans page template, when it renders, then it places the component with the two context values.

Given demo/settings.py, when the demonstration project runs, then MVP_PAYMENTS carries DRF_STRIPE_PRICING_TABLE_ID and DRF_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY with clearly-fake values, commented as a demonstration's rather than a project's.

Given demo/templates/base.html, when a demonstration page renders, then a provider_library block loads the provider's pricing-table library from the provider's own network and this package's own static file, with a comment saying the choice is the host project's; and the block can be emptied by a template that extends base.html.

Given docs/plans-page.md, when someone reads it, then they find the component, its attributes, the two settings the Plans page reads, and the statement that loading the provider's library is the project's own responsibility — and every example on the page runs against this branch.
